page_context_first_three_paragraphs: Killerwatts are Slayer monsters located in the Killerwatt plane , accessible through a portal at the top floor of Draynor Manor after completion of Ernest the Chicken . A Slayer level of 37 is required to kill them.

If a player is not wearing a pair of insulated boots while fighting them, both their Ranged and Melee attacks will have a much higher maximum hit. Even when wearing insulated boots, their attacks are still rapid and highly accurate, and they have an attack range of 13 tiles, meaning it is not possible to safespot them with long ranged weapons. A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Killerwatt plane .
Killerwatts are a commonly skipped Slayer task due to their relatively high damage output combined with their mediocre drops, except for those seeking their unique air diamond drop.

page_context_first_three_paragraphs: Molanisks are Slayer monsters that require level 39 Slayer to kill giving 52 Slayer experience per kill. A Slayer bell is necessary to initiate combat with them. Since they are only found in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon , completion of Death to the Dorgeshuun is required to fight molanisks and it is advisable to bring a light source . Molanisks do unusually low damage, meaning a player with half-decent armour should easily be able to kill them with no trouble.
They are mainly hunted for their earth emerald drop, or as a Slayer assignment from Vannaka .

Molanisks are found attached to cave walls and must be lured off with a Slayer bell to allow players to attack them. The Slayer bell only works within 3 tiles of the wall the molanisk is attached to. When lured off the wall, they are aggressive towards the player who lured them off with the bell. Molanisks respawn relatively quickly, so players who want to conserve run energy can just stay at the same respawn location. Alternatively, there is a spot south of the fairy ring with two spawns close together.

page_context_first_three_paragraphs: Infernal Mages are Slayer monsters that require 45 Slayer to kill. They are mainly hunted for their unique drops: the fire ruby , and the rare dark mystic boots and hat drops, and are sometimes hunted for their frequent drops of death runes . Players who plan on fighting them should be wary of their accurate magic attack, although Protect from Magic negates this completely.

To reach the Infernal Mage area in the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Slayer Tower , players can take the long way up the south-east stairs, which requires running past aggressive Banshees , so wearing Earmuffs or a Slayer helmet is recommended. Players with 18 Agility can avoid the banshees by using the broken window shortcut for quick access to the stairs.
Drop rates are estimated based on 31,289 samples from the Drop Rate Project , unless otherwise cited.

page_context_first_three_paragraphs: Sea snake hatchlings are found in the Miscellania and Etceteria dungeon , which can be entered during and after the Royal Trouble quest. A Slayer level of 40 is required to receive a sea snakes Slayer task, but they can be killed at any level. The snakes are poisonous , with the poison starting at 5 damage. Players fighting them should bring poison protection of some sort, such as an antipoison , antipoison+ , or antipoison++ . They attack with Melee and are vulnerable to Magic , particularly earth spells . Their unique drop is the water sapphire , which is shared with the sea snake young .

Players can use the blue eggs halfway through the tunnel as a safespot , although it is hard to get them to the player due to being a little further away than the sea snake young . A Dwarf multicannon can be used, but with reduced effectiveness due to the area being single-way combat .
The following drop rates are provided by Jagex, unless otherwise specified.

page_context_first_three_paragraphs: Jellies are Slayer monsters found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon and Wilderness Slayer Cave that require a Slayer level of 52 to kill. They give 75 Slayer experience per kill and drop hard clue scrolls and steel weaponry . Jellies and their variants are the only creatures to drop mithril boots .

They attack with magical acids that bypass physical defences [ 1 ] (a magic-based melee attack); therefore high magic defence armour, such as dragonhide is effective against their attacks. However, Protect from Melee will prevent all damage from them.

In the Wilderness cave jellies may only be attacked while on a Slayer task . Here they can be safespotted by using either side of the rockfall in the southern part of the cave, which the Jellies will not wander away from. It is also possible to safespot them by standing on the corner of the rocks in the western section of the chamber or from behind the stones in the hallway south of the jelly chamber.

page_context_first_three_paragraphs: Mogres are Slayer monsters and a type of ogre that are found in Mudskipper Point , requiring level 32 Slayer to kill. Mogres appear when disturbed by the player, who must lure them using Fishing explosives on an Ominous Fishing Spot . Previously, they could only be killed by players who had completed the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest . Since the release of Sailing , Mogres swimming in the ocean can now be killed with cannons from the player's boat. Doing so does not require completion of Skippy and the Mogres and does not demand the use of Fishing explosives, but still requires having level 32 Slayer.

Mogres can only be "lured" by clicking Use on the fishing explosives in your inventory, then clicking on the ominous fishing spots while also standing a few tiles away. Although the ominous fishing spots do have an options to "Lure" or "Bait", both these options do nothing (even with fishing explosives) and instead merely say in chat "Something seems to have scared all the fishes away..."
Mogres are usually killed by players searching for their unique drops of flippers or Mudskipper hats .
